subject: dependency-isolation-doctrine
meaning: The system is built in isolation; capabilities are consumed as pinned dependencies (crate-like); repair is upstream-first — a needed, broken, or missing capability is fixed in its owning project and re-pinned here; local forks and vendor patches prohibited; unavoidable divergence is a typed owner-authorized deviation with the upstream fix as reversal trigger.

directive: Checkout the text editors in text-diff-tool, wysiwig-editor, stone-oven and zachshallbetter. 'I've built quite a few over the years.' 'My personal site has live editing, editors, ai gen, etc.' 'We can do it better, but use the resources we have.'
interpretation: Not a licence to copy code in. The dependency doctrine already canonized (DESIGN.md 12.1) governs this exactly: capabilities are consumed as pinned dependencies, and anything needed, broken or missing is fixed UPSTREAM in the owning project and re-pinned -- never forked or vendor-patched here. 'We can do it better' authorizes improving those upstreams, not shadowing them with a local rewrite. The improvement this project is positioned to make is SH-16: an editor derived from a ResolvedSurface rather than hand-authored, so the authoring UI can be expressed more than one way. That is a genuine advance over a hand-built editor and does not require discarding one.
consequence: Editor work is now upstream-first. Each surveyed project is assessed as a dependency candidate with an explicit consumability verdict, following the SCMS-004 ledger pattern (pin-now / service-only / repair-first / violation). SCMS-044 (route the editor through the surface pipeline) is the local work; anything the editors themselves need is an upstream change with a deviation if it cannot wait.
openQuestion: The owner's site already does live editing, AI generation and an owner-gated write path against Neon Postgres. If that write path is materially better than what SCMS-041/043 built, the honest conclusion may be that semantic-cms should adopt it rather than replace it -- that is an owner decision, not an implementer's, and it will be raised once the surveys land.

directive: Owner revised the SSS formulation: 'SSS determines what semantic surface should exist for a given purpose/context' is too broad and would duplicate SES. Narrowed to a renderer-neutral SELECTION AND ASSEMBLY layer that does not determine graphical expression, presentation morphology, interaction authority, canonical truth, or empirical interpretation. MorphologyPolicy removed from SSS vocabulary. Requested SSS become an independent formal resource consumable by more than one project.
finding: VERIFIED ALREADY SATISFIED, at both the specification and implementation layers -- no change required. (1) The pinned upstream spec at _Protocols/semantic-surface-model docs/SSS-SPECIFICATION.md already carries the narrowed abstract verbatim ('what should participate in a surface, under what context, in what semantic organization, and why'), already lists graphical morphology / visual language / theme / recipe / appearance / rendering / persistent mutation among what SSS does not own, and already states SSS-INV-008 (semantic priority does not prescribe graphical presentation), SSS-INV-009 (SSS does not own graphical morphology) and SSS-INV-010 (operation exposure does not imply permission or execution). (2) No MorphologyPolicy term exists anywhere upstream. (3) The implementation conforms: impl/surface-resolver contains zero morphology vocabulary of any kind, while impl/surface-expression owns it entirely -- each adapter chooses its own container form per group, which is why the S3 vectors can assert that two expressions of one surface differ in morphology while preserving subjects, order and operations. (4) SSS is already an independent formal resource pinned by semantic-cms (SCMS-008), packaged as @semantic-systems/surface with schemas and conformance vectors, not an SCMS-local abstraction.
consequence: No upstream revision raised. The owner's re-derivation matches the landed boundary, which is a confirmation of the SPS morphologyFor decomposition made during SCMS-008 (selection and evidence tone to SSS; container form to the expression recipe). Recorded so the question is not re-opened from memory a third time.
residual: The one thing the owner's formulation adds that is worth carrying upstream eventually is the compact four-line operational distinction -- Domain: what exists. SSS: what matters here. SES: how it may appear. ICP: what may happen. That is clearer than anything currently in the spec's front matter and would be a PATCH-level editorial change under the SSS versioning policy, not a normative one.

directive: On adopting zach-core's working_copy draft buffer: 'Define it and we'll add it in at the appropriate time.' Definition requested; implementation deliberately deferred.
response: Defined in work/SCMS-044.md, state 'Defined - not scheduled', not claimed. Defining it surfaced a live defect rather than merely a missing feature: content.revise@1 inherits publicationState from the prior envelope, and reader surfaces resolve from journal.current(), so an in-progress edit to a promoted subject reaches the public immediately. Demonstrated against landed code -- a public reader's surface went from 'The Finished Version' to 'half-finished thought I was still' on a single revise. That contradicts section 6's claim that publishing is qualification plus promotion and never a boolean, so it is recorded as SH-15 in its own right rather than as a footnote.
designDecision: zach-core's mutable working_copy jsonb column cannot be copied -- an overwritten-in-place buffer is exactly the destructive edit section 3.4 forbids. The mechanism was re-derived instead: a working copy is an OBSERVATION, not a revision. Section 8.3's chip already names the state ('local, unsent') and section 8.4 already makes presence and soft locks observed envelopes with mandatory expires_at. Landing a draft as observed rather than declared yields every required property structurally: it cannot move a state axis (no-promotion rule), never reaches a reader surface (freeze projects only Content and Relation bodies), self-releases when abandoned (expiry), and states honestly what it is.
orderingConsequence: This should land BEFORE the P7 workload, not after. Today every landed autosave is a revision, so P7's free-lane overlap statistic would count autosave races as concurrent authorship. With buffering, only commits are revisions, and the overlap figure then measures what section 8.5 actually asked about. Running the workload first would produce a number that looks like evidence and is not.
awaitingOwner: The proposed DESIGN.md 8.9 passage is written but NOT applied; ratification is owner authority. SH-14 should also be resolved or deliberately left standing first, since the definition leans on freeze() not projecting observations -- currently true by omission rather than by declared intent, and leaning on an accident is how the last four negative results happened.

directive: Owner supplied three UI mockups as design direction for the CMS: two of an article editor and one of a page builder. No accompanying text -- the images are the specification.
whatTheyEstablish: The inspector is TABBED as Inspector / Surface (SSS) / Expression (SES). That is CANON != SURFACE != EXPRESSION rendered as interface structure rather than described in prose -- the separation becomes something a person navigates.

Status is labelled 'Multi-Axis' and shows Semantic / Evidence / Publication / Delivery as four independent rows. This confirms the section 3.5 no-collapse rule as a visible UI commitment, and matches what SCMS-040 already built.

Identity shows Subject ID, Revision with a 'not promoted' badge beside a draft number, Updated, and Schema with an explicit version (scms:article@1.2.0). Publication is visibly not a property of having saved.
The provenance chip appears as 'Live, checked 18s ago' in the top bar -- the SCMS-035 rule in its intended position.
A snapshot indicator sits in the sidebar: 'snap-001 (frozen)' in one mockup and 'snap-001 (live), Synced 18s ago' in the other. The freeze is a first-class, visible object.
Publishing is a nav SECTION containing Qualification (badge 5), Promotion (badge 2), Embargoes, and Delivery -- the qualification/promotion split and the delivery axis as places, not as fields.
Entitlement panel shows Minimum Access, Entitled Groups, and Staged Access -- richer than the single minimumAccess we implement.
Relations are grouped by type with counts: supports 4, references 9, part-of 2, contradicts 1, same-creator 7.
An Evidence tab with a count sits beside Relations and History.

The page builder tags each block with an SSS role (primary / supporting) shown as a corner badge, and its inspector splits Surface (SSS) -- Role, Priority, Evidence Tone -- from Expression (SES) -- Recipe, Theme, Variant. Evidence Tone is SPS's contribution surfaced directly in the authoring UI.
The footer states the whole dependency stack: Schema scms-0.1, Resolver @semantic-systems/surface v0.1.0, Expression SES, Consistency HCML, Protocol rr-rsp.
agreesWithBuilt: The multi-axis status, the chip's wording and position, the not-promoted badge, and the frozen-snapshot concept all match what SCMS-035/040/044 landed. The mockup is not a redirection of the architecture; it is the architecture made navigable.
gapsItNames: Surface(SSS) and Expression(SES) inspector panels are not exposed by the editor view-model even though the data exists; Evidence Tone has no implementation (SPS morphologyFor's evidence-density half); Recipe/Theme/Variant have no vocabulary in our expression adapters, which choose morphology directly; Entitled Groups and Staged Access are P2, deferred; Embargoes have no representation at all; the page builder is an SES composition surface with no counterpart in the codebase.
notRatified: These are design direction, not a canonical amendment. Nothing in DESIGN.md changes on the strength of a mockup, and the items above are recorded as gaps rather than accepted as scope.

directive: 'Yeah, lets do that. Migrate off of zach-core entirely.' Owner decision to stop depending on the zach-core codebase and API, and to give Semantic CMS its own persistence, auth and delivery.
whatThisSettles: SH-1, the open persistence-engine decision, is answered: Postgres, which DESIGN.md 13's non-normative sketch already named -- 'Store: Postgres. Revision and receipt tables append-only by grant (no UPDATE/DELETE for the runtime role). Logical decoding feeds the notify phase.' This is implementing an existing sketch rather than choosing afresh.
correctionToMyEarlierClaim: I told the owner the design had 'chosen Postgres without saying so'. It says so in section 13. I had read section 8.1's 'the store's native notification channel' and inferred what section 13 states outright.
dependencyPosture: Zero runtime dependencies was never canonical -- it appears in no canonical document, and was an implementation property of the narrow path. A Postgres driver is therefore a normal pinned dependency under the section 12.1 doctrine, not a deviation. It will be recorded as this project's first runtime dependency with its pin, so the crossing is deliberate and visible.
whatBecomesUnnecessary: The cache-tag purge protocol between two Vercel projects (section 8.3's invalidation over the channel replaces it, and the outbox already exists); the two-repository split; and SCMS-029's seed-versus-authoritative reconciliation, since there would be one store rather than a markdown seed and a Postgres system of record that have diverged.
whatMustBeBuilt: Authentication is the largest gap -- semantic-cms has none, and zach-core provides scrypt password hashing, signed expiring sessions, two separately revocable bearer tokens and constant-time comparison. That is SH-2. Also hosting, TLS, backups, and a migration runner, which zach-core does not have either (it re-runs a declarative schema file), so it is a gap inherited rather than solved.
prerequisite: SH-23 first. supersede() and revoke() currently rewrite stored rows, which cannot survive the no-UPDATE grant section 3.4 and section 13 both prescribe. Deriving them instead is small work now and structural work later; doing it during the persistence build is how a store quietly acquires an UPDATE grant 'just for the metadata'.
protectedActionsUnchanged: Building the store is implementation. Pointing zachshallbetter.com at it, decommissioning zach-core, and handling any production credentials remain protected actions requiring the owner's authorization at the time. I will not take them as implied by this directive.

designNote: Static and realtime are not in tension: section 8.3 makes static the committed snapshot baseline and realtime the invalidation layered on it. A static page is a materialized expression named by its surface fingerprint, which is access-safe by construction because the fingerprint is computed over the ACCESSIBLE dependency set. canon_blob (SCMS-060) is already the right home for it -- bytes named by their own hash, immutable by grant. The keystroke-churn problem that content-addressing would otherwise create is solved by the working copy (SCMS-045): drafts are observations, so they mint no revision, no fingerprint and no artifact; only a commit does. That is the second independent reason SCMS-045 should land early.
